A pipe under that floor block then puts water in through the outlets and takes it out through the strainers, and their current acts where they sit.
info.bettacraft.butterwort:
A flat rosette of sticky, yellow-green leaves that catch tiny insects, with violet flowers on thin stalks.
Swamp and shore: 50-100 % humidity, 15-30 °C, medium light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in swamps and mangroves.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.cabinet:
Made from any planks or stone (with the slabs of the same stone). Put a tank on it.
Holds an external filter (with two heaters) and nine stacks the feeder can use.
The button "Outlet" in its menu chooses the tank wall the filter hose goes up: back (default), left, right or front. Jet, bubbles and the current follow it; in front of the outlet the water moves faster (seahorses mind it, corals like it). Broken, the cabinet keeps the setting.
Cabinets side by side make one front: drawers at both ends, double doors between them. The button "Front" in the menu fixes the front of one cabinet, the small button next to it switches the dark joints.
info.bettacraft.calcium_additive:
Calcium for the skeletons of the stony corals (hammer coral, Lobophyllia, Acropora).
They use it up as they grow; below 380 mg/L they slow down, below 250 they stop.
Right-click a reef tank. Sea water and sea salt bring calcium too.
info.bettacraft.calcium_canister:
Calcium solution for the dosing pump. Stony corals use calcium to build their skeletons.
Dose calcium and alkalinity in about equal mL.
info.bettacraft.calcium_reactor:
The calcium reactor of a reef tank: tank water runs through a column of coral rubble that CO2 dissolves, and brings calcium and alkalinity (KH) back for the stony corals.
Place it next to a salt water tank, the cabinet of its sump, or on a pipe to the tanks; a CO2 gas cylinder next to it. Coral rubble in (by hand or hopper). It holds the calcium at about 440 mg/L.
info.bettacraft.ceramic_rings: Filter medium (biological): 24 water blocks per chamber, home of the bacteria. Clogs slowly; wash it in a water cauldron.
info.bettacraft.chaetomorpha:
Spaghetti algae for the refugium of a sump: with a tank light in the refugium they take up nitrate, starve the algae on the glass of nutrients and grow (up to 16).
Take the extra ones out: food for shrimp and snails, a vegetable for the food maker, or into the composter. Sold by the wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.christmas_moss:
A moss whose flat fronds stand in tiers like little fir trees.
Plant it in a tank interior on any solid block. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 8 days to full size with little light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in rivers, sometimes the aquarium net in rivers; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out.
info.bettacraft.clip_feeder:
A small automatic feeder that hangs on the side of the glass, at the top edge of a tank (for a tank whose top is taken by the light, e.g. one block high).
Place it on a side face of a top tank block. Right-click with food: fills it (one stack); empty hand: 1, 2 or 3 feedings a day; sneak + empty hand: takes the food out.
No hopper; it does not cover the water against evaporation. The big feeder on top of the tank comes first if there is one.
info.bettacraft.co2_cylinder:
CO2 gas cylinder with pressure regulator and bubble counter. Place it next to a tank or on it.
Right-click: 0 to 10 bubbles per second (sneak + mouse wheel too). A bigger tank needs more bubbles.
Plants grow much faster with CO2 (strong-light plants most) and the pH drops. Too much CO2 stresses and kills the animals, at night too when the plants take none up - use a solenoid valve.
Refill empty cylinders at a CO2 filling station. Broken, it keeps its gas.
info.bettacraft.co2_solenoid:
Right-click a CO2 cylinder to put it on: it closes the cylinder while the lights of the tank are off (its daylight timer, or the night).
Without it the CO2 keeps flowing at night, when the plants take none up.
info.bettacraft.co2_station:
Fills CO2 cylinders with the flue gas of a burning furnace, smoker, blast furnace or campfire next to it (on it, beside it or above it). More fires fill faster: about a day of burning for a full cylinder.
With a power option on its compressor also needs FE. CO2 gas of other mods (fluid tag #bettacraft:co2_gas) goes in through pipes.
Right-click with a cylinder to put it in, empty hand to take it out, sneak to see what it does. Hoppers take out full cylinders.
info.bettacraft.column_cactus:
A ribbed column with one or two arms bending upwards and woolly white tips.
Dry and hot: 10-55 % humidity, 20-38 °C, strong light. Plant it on sand, gravel or soil on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (offsets around it) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in deserts and badlands; from a cactus.
Shears: take an offset (a small rooted plant).
info.bettacraft.cooler_large: Cools up to 64 water blocks. Place it in the tank interior or into an external filter.
info.bettacraft.cooler_medium: Cools up to 32 water blocks. Place it in the tank interior or into an external filter.
info.bettacraft.cooler_small:
Cools up to 16 water blocks towards the target temperature of the tank when it is warmer around the tank (deserts, the Nether).
Place it in the tank interior (under water) or into an external filter. Coolers add up.
info.bettacraft.coral_rubble: Broken coral skeletons (calcium carbonate): the filling of the calcium reactor. From dead coral blocks or calcite.
info.bettacraft.corner_filter:
A motor filter for the tank interior, slim enough for a corner. Keeps 20 water blocks clean and moves the surface (oxygen).
Without an intake sponge it sucks in young animals. Right-click or sneak + mouse wheel: power regulator.
info.bettacraft.crank:
The crank winds devices with a spring: right-click, hold the button to keep winding (one charge, a day of a device's work, in about five seconds).
Without the power options only the food maker and the fertilizer maker need it. With a power option on also the external filter (with its heaters), the multiblock filter, the reverse osmosis unit, the water change controller, the water pump and the cabinet under a tank can be wound instead of FE; the cabinet holds six charges and gives them to every device of its tank.
info.bettacraft.critter_bucket:
Shrimp, crayfish, snails or hermit crabs of one species in a plain bucket of water (up to 32 small ones, 24 bigger ones).
Take them out of a tank in the tank menu (bucket button), or catch them in the world with a bucket of water.
Use it on a tank to put them in (with 1000 mB of water); poured out in the world they crawl off.
info.bettacraft.crucible:
Melts stainless steel: 4 iron ingots, coal and nether quartz give 3 ingots in 10 seconds.
Heat: lava, a lava cauldron or a magma block right under it (free), FE (power mods) or fuel: a lava bucket, a blaze rod or blaze powder. Hoppers fill it from above and the sides and empty it from below.
info.bettacraft.cryptocoryne_flamingo:
A rare crypt with whitish pink leaves that get brighter and pinker in strong light; slow.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate (the interior floor with a substrate, sand, gravel or dirt). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 14 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: rarely the aquarium net or fishing in swamps, rarely from the wandering trader; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out.
info.bettacraft.cryptocoryne_parva:
The smallest Cryptocoryne: narrow little leaves that slowly grow into a lawn by runners.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate (the interior floor with a substrate, sand, gravel or dirt). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 16 days to full size with little light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in rivers, sometimes the aquarium net in rivers; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it sends out runners.
info.bettacraft.cryptocoryne_wendtii_bro:
Brown-red wavy leaves, redder under strong light; sends out runners now and then.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate (the interior floor with a substrate, sand, gravel or dirt). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 9 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in swamps, sometimes in a bottle of swamp water or the aquarium net in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out.
info.bettacraft.cryptocoryne_wendtii_gre:
A rosette of green, slightly wavy leaves; sends out runners now and then.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate (the interior floor with a substrate, sand, gravel or dirt). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 9 days to full size with little light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in swamps, sometimes in a bottle of swamp water or the aquarium net in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out.
info.bettacraft.cushion_moss:
A pale green moss that grows into round, soft cushions on any surface.
Tropical and humid: 65-100 % humidity, 20-30 °C, little light. Plant it on any solid block on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (it creeps on) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in the lush caves and swamps; from a moss block; from the wandering trader and the aquarist.
Shears: divide the clump (half of it as a plant); breaking a piece of the moss divides it too.
info.bettacraft.daphnia:
Daphnia (water fleas): live food for bettas, tankmates, frogs and seahorses.
A bottle of swamp water sometimes brings up a few: put them into a daphnia barrel to start a culture.
info.bettacraft.daphnia_barrel:
Breeds daphnia. Fill it with at least 2 buckets of water, put daphnia in and feed yeast or green water. It needs light 9 or more and no hot sun (shade in the desert).
Harvest with the aquarium net, a hopper or a live food pump before it gets crowded, or the culture collapses.
info.bettacraft.decor:
A decoration structure: places a small build facing you.
Works in a tank interior (it then shows up in the tank in miniature) and anywhere in the world.
info.bettacraft.dosing_canister: Empty canister of the dosing pump. Fill it in the crafting grid: calcium (two calcium additives), alkalinity (calcite and two dried kelp), magnesium (two sea salt and a prismarine shard) or trace elements (sea salt, prismarine crystals and a glow ink sac).
info.bettacraft.dosing_pump:
Dosing pump for a reef tank ("Balling light"): four channels, each with a canister and its mL per day.
Place it next to a salt water tank, or join it to pipes that lead into tanks (several tanks share the dose). Right-click: canisters in, mL per day with - and + (sneak: by 10), what it does and the values of the tank.
It only doses into salt water. Hoppers put full canisters in and take empty ones out.
info.bettacraft.drive_adapter:
Only with Create. Set it on a tank wall or under a tank (its plate on the tank, the shaft away from it) and connect a Create shaft, cogwheel or motor to its shaft: the rotation charges the tank's FE buffer, so every device of the tank that takes the tank's FE runs on it (filters, flow pumps and skimmers, heaters, coolers and heat mats, lights, air pumps, misters).
64 RPM give the full power (256 FE/t), slower proportionally. Several adapters on one tank add up to a limit (1024 FE/t).
It costs real stress: the more the devices need (and while the buffer fills), the more SU; turning without load costs a little. An overstressed network gives the tank nothing.
The cabinet under a tank takes a shaft too: set its side in the cabinet menu.
info.bettacraft.duckweed:
A floating plant for the water surface of a tank. Use it on a tank: it floats where you look at the water.
Duckweed grows fastest and takes up waste from the water. With light (a lit tank light or daylight) and nutrients (the waste of the animals) it forms offshoots until the surface is covered (60 % by default).
Find it: fill a glass bottle with swamp water (sometimes a bit of duckweed comes up), fishing in swamps.
Take plants out: right-click the surface with an empty hand or an aquarium net; net + sneak thins the whole tank out by half.
info.bettacraft.dwarf_frog_bucket:
A dwarf clawed frog in a bucket of water. Use it on a tank to put the frog in (with 1000 mB of water).
Frogs live on the bottom and swim up to breathe: the tank needs air above the water (the air gap below the glass, or a tank that is not full).
They eat mosquito larvae, artemia and sinking pellets, but slowly: bettas snatch it away. Sneak + right-click with food feeds the frogs directly.
Catch frogs with the aquarium net in swamps and jungle water, or buy one from the wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.echeveria:
A succulent rosette of plump, blue-grey leaves whose tips blush pink in strong light.
Dry and hot: 10-55 % humidity, 20-38 °C, strong light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (offsets around it) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in deserts and badlands; from the wandering trader and the aquarist.
Shears: take an offset (a small rooted plant).
info.bettacraft.echinodorus_red_diamond:
A compact sword plant with wine-red leaves, the redder the stronger the light.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate (the interior floor with a substrate, sand, gravel or dirt). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 8 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in jungles, sometimes the aquarium net in jungle water; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out.
info.bettacraft.eleocharis_acicularis:
Hairgrass: a lawn of thin, upright needles that spreads by runners.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 3.5 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in swamps, sometimes the aquarium net in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it sends out runners.
info.bettacraft.external_filter:
Place it next to a tank (facing it) or put it into a cabinet under the tank.
Keeps 32 water blocks clean and holds two heaters or coolers of any size.
info.bettacraft.feeder:
Place it on top of a tank and fill it with food (also by hopper).
Feeds 1 to 3 times a day, picks fry food for fry and takes food from cabinets under the tank.
info.bettacraft.fertilizer_canister: A canister of liquid fertilizer for the dosing pump (500 mL, two bottles). The pump doses it into fresh and salt water tanks, its mL per day.
info.bettacraft.fertilizer_maker:
Mixes a kelp meal and a nutrient salt with 250 mB of water into 250 mB of liquid fertilizer (a bottle). Water comes from a bucket, a pipe or other mods.
Empty glass bottles in the bottle slot are filled; otherwise the fertilizer goes into pipes or a tank next to it (a tank takes it only up to 100 %).
Without power it runs on a spring: wind it with the crank. With a power option on it takes FE, and its spring when the FE is short; Create's rotation drives it too. Redstone pauses it.
info.bettacraft.filter_chamber:
Part of the multiblock external filter: holds one filter medium. Join chambers face to face (1 to 16), put the pump head on them and an inlet and an outlet against them.
Right-click with a medium: put it in; empty hand: take it out.
info.bettacraft.filter_foam: Filter medium (mechanical): 12 water blocks per chamber. Clogs fastest; a clogged sponge also slows the flow. Wash it in a water cauldron.
info.bettacraft.filter_inlet: Where the water goes into the multiblock filter: place it against a chamber; the blue socket joins a pipe or a tank.
info.bettacraft.filter_outlet: Where the water leaves the multiblock filter: place it against a chamber; the orange socket joins a pipe or a tank.
info.bettacraft.filter_peat: Filter medium: 6 water blocks per chamber; softens the water and lowers the pH. Used up slowly.
info.bettacraft.filter_pump_head:
The pump of the multiblock external filter: pulls water through the inlet and pushes it out of the outlet. When both lead to the same tank it cleans that tank by its media.
Right-click: the filter's screen. Sneak + mouse wheel: power regulator.
info.bettacraft.fish_bag:
Right-click a small fish to catch it. A bag holds the fish and 100 mB of water.
It takes every small water animal, also of other mods and those without a bucket (squids).
Use it on a tank to put the fish in, or take a fish out in the tank menu.
A bag holds several animals of one species, half of what a bucket holds (e.g. 16 shrimp, 12 rasboras, 1 betta).
Reusable; empty bags stack to 16.
info.bettacraft.fish_flakes:
Fish flakes: float at the surface. A favourite of the midwater fish (tetras, rasboras, livebearers, gouramis); bottom fish hardly get any.
Made in the food maker.
info.bettacraft.fittonia:
A low, bushy plant of the shade with dark leaves netted with pale veins; it wilts quickly in dry air.
Tropical and humid: 65-100 % humidity, 20-30 °C, little light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (side shoots) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: on the floor of jungles; from the wandering trader and the aquarist.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.flame_moss:
A moss that grows in upright, twisted tufts like little green flames.
Plant it in a tank interior on any solid block. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 8 days to full size with little light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in rivers, sometimes the aquarium net in rivers; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out.
info.bettacraft.flow_pump:
Moves the water of a reef tank: corals need flow (Acropora a lot, mushrooms little).
Place it in the tank interior under water like the internal filter. Uses the power of the filters if they need power.
info.bettacraft.food_granules:
Food granules: sink slowly, so the bottom fish (corydoras, loaches) get their share even next to fast fish. Their favourite.
Made in the food maker.
info.bettacraft.food_maker:
Makes fish food in batches: pellets, flakes, granules, algae wafers, shrimp food, fry powder and frozen food (live food with ice) from wheat, kelp, fish, spider eyes, sugar, eggs and vegetables.
Choose the product with < and > or leave it on Automatic. Without power it runs on a spring: right-click it with the crank to wind it (hold the button; a full spring lasts a day); with a power option on it takes FE, and its spring when the FE is short.
Hoppers and storage mods put ingredients in from every side and take the food out.
info.bettacraft.frozen_artemia:
Frozen artemia: eaten like live food by juveniles and older (not by fry); a favourite of the bettas and seahorses.
Made in the food maker from artemia nauplii and ice.
info.bettacraft.frozen_daphnia:
Frozen daphnia: eaten like live food; a favourite of the bettas and the midwater fish.
Made in the food maker from daphnia and ice.
info.bettacraft.frozen_mosquito_larvae:
Frozen mosquito larvae: eaten like live food (juveniles and older) and a favourite of the bettas, bottom fish and seahorses; it keeps and conditions for breeding.
Made in the food maker from live food and ice; cannot be pumped.
info.bettacraft.fry_powder:
Fine powder food: feeds the fry of every species (bettas and tankmates) through the whole fry stage.
Crafted from two betta pellets and bone meal.
info.bettacraft.glass_pipe: The cheap pipe for everything: carries water with all its values (temperature, salt, quality, nitrate) between tanks, filters, reservoirs and the tanks and pipes of other mods: 50 mB/t. It joins every neighbour that fits on every side; the pipe wrench closes a side. At a filter's inlet or outlet it becomes its intake or return line (coloured rings); a filter line carries at most what its weakest pipe carries. Sneak-right-click a pipe with it: both run in one block (a bundle, up to four). Placed in a tank interior it is an interior pipe. Pipes do not pump: a water pump, a filter pump head or another mod's pump moves the water.
info.bettacraft.golden_barrel_cactus:
A squat, ribbed ball of a cactus with a crown of golden spines; grows very slowly.
Dry and hot: 10-55 % humidity, 20-38 °C, strong light. Plant it on sand, gravel or soil on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (offsets around it) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in deserts and badlands.
Shears: take an offset (a small rooted plant).
info.bettacraft.green_star_polyps:
Soft coral: glowing green polyps on a purple mat; grows fast and overgrows the rock.
On reef rock in a reef tank. Light: medium, flow: medium, no calcium.
Frag it with shears; wild colonies grow on the warm ocean reefs (shears cut frags off them), more frags from the aquarium net on a reef, vanilla corals or the wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.green_water_bottle: Green water full of algae: food for the daphnia barrel (more than yeast). The empty bottle stays with you.
info.bettacraft.green_water_culture: Swamp water with bone meal: in the light it turns into green water after a day (in the inventory or dropped).
info.bettacraft.guzmania:
A bromeliad with glossy green leaves and a star of orange bracts on a short stalk in its middle. Its cup holds water for the tadpoles of the dart frogs.
Tropical and humid: 65-100 % humidity, 20-30 °C, medium light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (offsets around it) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: on the floor of jungles; from the wandering trader.
Shears: take an offset (a small rooted plant).
info.bettacraft.hammer_coral:
Stony coral (LPS, Euphyllia ancora): skeleton branches with fleshy, hammer-shaped heads.
On reef rock in a reef tank. Light: medium, flow: medium, needs calcium.
Frag it with shears; wild colonies grow on the warm ocean reefs (shears cut frags off them), rarely a piece from the aquarium net on a reef, or from vanilla corals.
info.bettacraft.haworthia:
A small succulent with pointed, dark green leaves banded with white warts; content with less light.
Dry and hot: 10-55 % humidity, 20-38 °C, medium light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (offsets around it) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in deserts and badlands; from the wandering trader.
Shears: take an offset (a small rooted plant).
info.bettacraft.heater_large: Heats up to 64 water blocks. Place it in the tank interior or into an external filter.
info.bettacraft.heater_medium: Heats up to 32 water blocks. Place it in the tank interior or into an external filter.
info.bettacraft.heater_small:
Heats up to 16 water blocks towards the target temperature of the tank (default 27 °C).
Place it in the tank interior (under water) or into an external filter. Heaters add up.
info.bettacraft.hemianthus_callitrichoid:
The finest carpet of all: tiny, bright green leaves in a dense cushion. Needs very strong light and grows well only with CO2.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 4 days to full size with very strong light (an LED panel or a high-power LED), nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: rarely when fishing in rivers, rarely the aquarium net in rivers; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it sends out runners.
info.bettacraft.high_power_led:
The strongest light tier: a planted-tank light with a heat sink that joins with its neighbours on all four sides into one fixture of any size. Light 15 plus 5 on the part of the tank it covers.
Dye it like the light bar; dimmer and daylight timer in the tank menu (tab Devices).
info.bettacraft.hornwort:
Hornwort (Ceratophyllum demersum) has no roots: its shoots with whorls of stiff leaves float free just under the surface and hang deep into the water. Grows fast and takes up the most waste. Use it on a tank: it floats where you look at the water.
Grows with light and nutrients, forms offshoots and takes up waste.
Find it: fishing in swamps and mangrove swamps.
Take plants out: right-click the surface with an empty hand or an aquarium net; net + sneak thins the whole tank out by half.
info.bettacraft.hygrophila_pinnatifida:
Deeply lobed, olive brown leaves, reddish under strong light; roots in the substrate and also on stone and wood.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate or on stone and wood; grows up to the water surface. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 5 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in rivers, sometimes the aquarium net in rivers; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it forms side shoots; at the surface it shades the tank.
info.bettacraft.infusoria: First food for fry. One bottle feeds 20 fry. Hand feeding gives the bottle back.
info.bettacraft.infusoria_culture: Turns into a bottle of infusoria after one in-game day, in your inventory, a chest or on the ground.
info.bettacraft.intake_guard: A fine mesh over the opening of a filter intake in the tank: it keeps the animals out. Every dock of a filter inlet line needs one (or an intake strainer) behind it. Use it on the glass where the pipe docks, or place it in the interior next to the pipe dock or at the end of interior pipes from it.
info.bettacraft.intake_sponge: Use it on a motor filter (internal or corner filter in the interior, external filter, cabinet with a filter): it covers the intake and the filter no longer sucks in young animals. It comes back when the filter is broken.
info.bettacraft.intake_strainer: The intake in the tank interior: water pumped out through the bulkhead leaves the tank here (a gentle pull towards it).
info.bettacraft.internal_filter:
Place it in the tank interior: a filter tower with a visible water jet.
While it stands under water it keeps 16 water blocks clean (water quality) and moves the surface (oxygen). Without an intake sponge it sucks in young animals. Right-click or sneak + mouse wheel: power regulator.
info.bettacraft.java_fern:
A robust fern with long, lance-shaped fronds on a creeping rhizome.
Plant it in a tank interior on stone or wood (rocks, roots, decoration). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 12 days to full size with little light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in jungles and rivers; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Break a rhizome piece to divide it (half of it as an item).
info.bettacraft.java_moss:
Fine moss that spreads in a cushion over stone, wood and the floor.
Plant it in a tank interior on any solid block. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 6 days to full size with little light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: shears on a moss block next to water (lush caves), sometimes the aquarium net in rivers and jungle water; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out.
info.bettacraft.kelp_meal: Dried kelp ground with bone meal: the organic part of liquid fertilizer. Goes into the fertilizer maker.
info.bettacraft.large_net: Large net for big animals (giant catfish, sharks, rays, dolphins). Right-click a wild big animal with an empty transport tub in your inventory to catch it; swung in open water it now and then brings up a big animal of that water.
info.bettacraft.larva_tub:
Breeds mosquito larvae under the open sky.
Fill it with a water bucket (or a pipe) and add organic matter: leaves, wheat, rotten flesh or bone meal (also by hopper).
A batch takes about 2 days, faster at night, in swamps and in the rain. Harvest with a glass bottle or let a hopper below take the larvae.
info.bettacraft.leather_coral:
Soft coral (Sarcophyton): a thick stalk with a wide, cream coloured cap full of polyps.
On reef rock in a reef tank. Light: medium, flow: medium, no calcium.
Frag it with shears; wild colonies grow on the warm ocean reefs (shears cut frags off them), rarely a piece from the aquarium net on a reef, or from vanilla corals.
info.bettacraft.led_panel:
The middle light tier: one item lays a panel two blocks wide; panels in a row join into one long panel. Light 15 plus 2.5 on the part of the tank it covers: red plants get redder, strong-light plants (Monte Carlo, Alternanthera) grow faster, and without CO2 and fertiliser the algae too.
Dye it like the light bar; dimmer and daylight timer in the tank menu (tab Devices).
Directly on a tank it covers the blocks under it like a lid: no evaporation, nothing gets in or out there.
info.bettacraft.level_sensor:
Next to a tank (or a multiblock filter): tops off evaporated water from a reservoir, pipe, other mod's tank or water source next to it. Fresh water only: in a reef tank the salt stays behind, so fresh water keeps the salinity where it was.
Right-click: target level 100 to 50 %.
info.bettacraft.lily_pipe: A glass outlet in the tank interior: spreads the water softly just under the surface. Its mouth points the way you look when you place it.
info.bettacraft.limnophila_sessiliflora:
Soft, feathery whorls of light green leaves; grows fast and is undemanding.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate; grows up to the water surface. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 2.5 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in swamps, sometimes the aquarium net in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it forms side shoots; at the surface it shades the tank.
info.bettacraft.liquid_fertilizer:
Five portions of liquid fertilizer. Right-click a tank: one portion goes into the water (a portion brings 4 water blocks to the right level).
Up to 100 % the aquarium and floating plants of Bettacraft grow up to half as fast again; they use it up. From 150 % the tank is overdosed and the algae grow faster. Water changes dilute it. Plants of other mods are not affected.
info.bettacraft.lithops:
Two fat leaves that look like a pebble, with a yellow flower from the cleft. Grows very slowly and rots in humid air.
Dry and hot: 10-45 % humidity, 20-38 °C, strong light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (offsets around it) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in deserts and badlands; rarely from the wandering trader.
Shears: take an offset (a small rooted plant).
info.bettacraft.live_food_pump:
Pumps live food from the breeder next to it (daphnia barrel, artemia hatchery, larva tub, tubifex dish) through the pipes into the tanks, on a schedule.
Right-click: doses per day, portions per dose and "Dose now". A tank only takes the food when somebody there eats it. Redstone pauses it.
info.bettacraft.live_rock:
Reef rock full of coralline algae and bacteria: in a salt water tank it cleans the water like a filter (no power needed).
Corals grow on it too. Craft it from reef rock and a coral, or buy it from the wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.lobophyllia:
Stony coral (LPS): a fleshy dome with meandering ridges, red and green.
On reef rock in a reef tank. Light: medium, flow: gentle, needs calcium.
Frag it with shears; wild colonies grow on the warm ocean reefs (shears cut frags off them), rarely a piece from the aquarium net on a reef, or from vanilla corals.
info.bettacraft.ludwigia_repens:
A fast stem plant with copper-red leaves, redder under strong light.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate; grows up to the water surface. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 3 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in swamps, sometimes in a bottle of swamp water; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it forms side shoots; at the surface it shades the tank.
info.bettacraft.ludwigia_super_red:
A Ludwigia bred for its colour: deep wine-red leaves, the reddest under strong light. Grows well only with CO2.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate; grows up to the water surface. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 3.5 days to full size with strong light (a lit tank light), nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: rarely when fishing in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it forms side shoots; at the surface it shades the tank.
info.bettacraft.magnesium_canister: Magnesium solution for the dosing pump. Magnesium falls slowly in every salt water tank; below 1150 mg/L calcium and alkalinity drop out and the stony corals grow slower.
info.bettacraft.magnifier:
Analyses the hidden genes of the animals in a tank.
Right-click a tank: every animal in it is analysed. In the tank menu the "Analyse" button analyses the selected fish or small animal.
New animals (caught, bought, born) do not show their hidden genes until they are analysed; the result stays with the animal in tanks, buckets and bags.
64 uses (one per animal), repaired at the anvil with glass panes.
Craft: a glass pane in a ring of copper or gold ingots on a stick.
info.bettacraft.mammillaria:
A small cactus that grows into a cluster of round heads, each with a ring of pink flowers.
Dry and hot: 10-55 % humidity, 20-38 °C, strong light. Plant it on sand, gravel or soil on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (offsets around it) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in deserts and badlands.
Shears: take an offset (a small rooted plant).
info.bettacraft.marcgravia:
A creeper whose small round leaves lie on stone and wood like shingles.
Tropical and humid: 65-100 % humidity, 20-30 °C, little light. Plant it on stone or wood on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: on the floor of jungles.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.marimo:
A velvety ball of green algae: grows extremely slowly, never minds cool water and lives practically forever. In the current of a filter or outlet it rolls slowly over the floor.
Put it in a tank interior on the floor or any solid block. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 60 days to full size with little light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 5-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: rarely when fishing in rivers, rarely the aquarium net in rivers; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. It rolls with the current (config features.aquaticPlants.marimoRolling).
info.bettacraft.marsilea_hirsuta:
Water clover: a slow carpet of small four-leaved clovers on thin stalks; content with little light.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 6 days to full size with little light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in swamps, sometimes the aquarium net in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it sends out runners.
info.bettacraft.mini_orchid:
A small orchid that sits on wood or stone, with a few broad leaves and an arching spike of pink flowers.
Tropical and humid: 65-100 % humidity, 20-30 °C, medium light. Plant it on stone or wood on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: on the floor of jungles; rarely from the wandering trader.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.mirror_stick:
Hold the mirror stick in either hand and look at a male betta (up to 6 blocks, also through the glass): it flares at its reflection, holds still and shows the mirror its side (bettas see sideways).
Mirror training: a male that flared at the mirror during the last day gets ready for a bubble nest a little faster (server config, 1.25x by default).
Craft: glass pane, iron nugget and stick, one above the other.
info.bettacraft.monitor:
A screen for your tanks. Monitors next to each other join into one screen of up to 8 x 5 blocks. It finds every tank within 32 blocks by itself, named after the tank sign. Right-click it to arrange the dashboard: values, traffic lights, graphs, animals, devices, alarms (with a redstone signal) and the log. Sneak and right-click for its state.
With a power option on it needs 1 FE per tick and block.
info.bettacraft.monte_carlo:
A carpet of tiny round leaves on the floor; spreads by runners; needs strong light.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 3 days to full size with strong light (a lit tank light), nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: the aquarium net in swamps and rivers, rarely fishing in rivers, the wandering trader; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it sends out runners.
info.bettacraft.mosquito_larvae:
Live food: one portion feeds up to 4 bettas and gets a breeding pair in the mood twice as fast.
From a smelted bottle of swamp water or a larva tub, sometimes from mud mined in a swamp.
info.bettacraft.mulm: Mulm: the dirt washed out of filter sponges and ceramic rings (clean them in a water cauldron). Food for the tubifex dish.
info.bettacraft.mushroom_coral:
Soft coral (Discosoma): flat red discs on short stalks, a few more over time.
On reef rock in a reef tank. Light: low, flow: gentle, no calcium.
Frag it with shears; wild colonies grow on the warm ocean reefs (shears cut frags off them), more frags from the aquarium net on a reef, vanilla corals or the wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.myriophyllum_red:
Feathery red whorls; needs strong light, CO2 and soft water.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate; grows up to the water surface. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 3 days to full size with strong light (a lit tank light), nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in swamps, sometimes the aquarium net in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it forms side shoots; at the surface it shades the tank.
info.bettacraft.needlegrass:
A bunchgrass of dry lands with fine blades and feathery seed awns. Tortoises graze it.
Dry and hot: 10-70 % humidity, 20-38 °C, strong light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in savannas; from a dead bush.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.neoregelia:
A bromeliad with a cup of broad strap leaves; its heart turns bright red, the more so in strong light. The cup holds water: dart frogs raise their tadpoles in it.
Tropical and humid: 65-100 % humidity, 20-30 °C, medium light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (offsets around it) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: on the floor of jungles; from the wandering trader and the aquarist.
Shears: take an offset (a small rooted plant).
info.bettacraft.nepenthes:
A carnivorous plant of the tropical highlands: from its leaves tendrils carry hanging pitchers with a lid. Likes it humid and not too warm.
Swamp and shore: 55-100 % humidity, 16-28 °C, medium light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: on the floor of jungles; rarely from the wandering trader.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.nozzle: An outlet in the tank interior: a narrow, strong jet (corals and seahorses notice it, fish swim into it).
info.bettacraft.nutrient_salt: Bone meal (phosphate), charcoal (potash) and iron: the minerals of liquid fertilizer. Goes into the fertilizer maker.
info.bettacraft.nymphaea_lotus_green:
The green form of the tiger lotus (Nymphaea lotus): green leaves with brown spots from a tuber; grown up it sends floating leaves to the surface.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 6 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in jungles, sometimes the aquarium net in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. The floating leaves shade the tank like floating plants.
info.bettacraft.outlet_guard: A mesh cap on a filter outlet in the tank: the animals cannot swim in. Every dock of a filter outlet line needs one (or a lily pipe, nozzle or spray bar) behind it. Use it on the glass where the pipe docks, or place it in the interior.
info.bettacraft.papyrus:
The tall sedge of the Nile: smooth culms with a mop of fine rays on top. Needs strong light.
Swamp and shore: 55-100 % humidity, 15-30 °C, strong light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (side shoots) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in swamps and mangroves.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.peperomia:
A small, bushy plant with round, glossy, fleshy leaves on reddish stems.
Tropical and humid: 65-100 % humidity, 20-30 °C, little light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (side shoots) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: on the floor of jungles.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.ph_test_kit:
Measures the pH of a tank (5 to 9) and shows where it is drifting.
Soil lowers the pH, limestone raises it; peat, almond leaves, driftwood and CO2 lower it.
Enough for 50 tests.
info.bettacraft.phytoplankton: Microalgae in salt water. Used on a reef tank it greens the water and keeps the rotifers in it alive (they eat it). The food of a rotifer culture.
info.bettacraft.phytoplankton_culture: Salt water with a sea plant and bone meal: turns into a bottle of phytoplankton after one in-game day, but only in light (level 9 or more).
info.bettacraft.pipe_cover: Hides filter pipes and pipe bundles. Hold it in the main hand and a full block (stone, planks, bricks, glass ...) in the off hand, then right-click a pipe: it is drawn as that block and is a full block to walk on, while its lines, T-pieces and connections stay as they were. One block is used and comes back when the cover comes off (sneak-right-click with the pipe cover) or the pipe is broken. The pipe cover itself is not used up. The facades of Applied Energistics 2, EnderIO conduit facades and Mekanism Covers can be used on the pipes directly, and the facades of the Cable Facades mod go on them as on any cable.
info.bettacraft.pipe_wrench: The pipe wrench closes and opens the sides of a pipe: right-click a side (an arm of the pipe, or the face of its middle where a side is closed). A closed side joins nothing and shows a cap; so two lines run side by side without joining, and joints are moved. On a bundle it works on the pipe you look at; sneak-right-click moves that pipe to the next spot of the bundle, to line it up with the next bundle. It is not used up.
info.bettacraft.pogostemon_helferi:
A low bush of crinkled, light green leaves; stays small. Grows well only with CO2.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate; stays low. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 6 days to full size with strong light (a lit tank light), nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in rivers, sometimes the aquarium net in rivers; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it forms side shoots.
info.bettacraft.pothos:
A climbing vine with heart-shaped, golden marbled leaves; it climbs up towards the lid and its tips trail down again. Robust and undemanding.
Tropical and humid: 65-100 % humidity, 20-30 °C, little light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (side shoots) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: on the floor of jungles; from the wandering trader and the aquarist.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.prickly_pear:
A cactus of flat pads standing on each other, with yellow flowers on the rim. Tortoises love its pads.
Dry and hot: 10-55 % humidity, 20-38 °C, strong light. Plant it on sand, gravel or soil on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (offsets around it) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in deserts, badlands and savannas.
Shears: take an offset (a small rooted plant).
info.bettacraft.protein_skimmer:
Foams the waste out of salt water: a strong extra filter for reef tanks (no effect in fresh water, there is no foam).
Hang it on a side of the tank like the external filter. Uses the power of the filters if they need power.
info.bettacraft.red_root_floater:
A rare floating plant with small round leaves and red roots. Under strong light (a lit tank light or full daylight) its leaves turn red, under weak light they stay green. Grows slowly.
Find it: rarely from the wandering trader, rarely when fishing in mangrove swamps.
Take plants out: right-click the surface with an empty hand or an aquarium net; net + sneak thins the whole tank out by half.
info.bettacraft.red_tiger_lotus:
Large red, mottled leaves from a tuber; grown up it sends floating leaves to the surface.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 6 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: the aquarium net in jungle water and swamps, rarely fishing in jungles and swamps, rarely from the wandering trader; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. The floating leaves shade the tank like floating plants.
info.bettacraft.reef_rock: Porous aragonite for the rock work of a reef tank. Corals and the anemone are glued onto it in the tank interior.
info.bettacraft.reindeer_lichen:
A lichen of pale, finely branched tufts (often sold as "lichen moss"); it dries out without harm and waits for moister days.
Tropical and humid: 40-100 % humidity, 10-26 °C, medium light. Plant it on any solid block on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (it creeps on) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in the lush caves.
Shears: divide the clump (half of it as a plant); breaking a piece of the moss divides it too.
info.bettacraft.remineralising_salt:
Raises the TDS of a tank: one portion adds 400 ppm to a bucket of water (config).
Sneaking adds as much as brings the tank to 150 ppm, the middle of the range of soft-water shrimp.
Not for salt water.
info.bettacraft.reservoir: Holds 16 buckets of water for the top-off and the water change controller. Fill it with buckets or pipes; any water mixes in. A comparator reads how full it is.
info.bettacraft.riccia_fluitans:
A liverwort of forked, bright green thalli: tied onto stone or wood it grows into a shining cushion, on the surface it floats; males like to build their bubble nest in it.
Tie it onto stone or wood in a tank interior (rocks, roots, decoration), or use it on a tank from outside: then it floats on the surface like a floating plant. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 4 days to full size with strong light (a lit tank light), nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in swamps, sometimes the aquarium net in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out.
info.bettacraft.ro_membrane:
The membrane of the reverse osmosis unit: about 128 buckets of RO water, then it is worn out.
Right-click the unit with it to put it in (the old one comes out).
info.bettacraft.ro_prefilter:
Sediment and carbon prefilter of the reverse osmosis unit: protects the membrane, about 32 buckets.
Right-click the unit with it to put it in (the old one comes out).
info.bettacraft.ro_unit:
Makes reverse osmosis water: nothing dissolved (TDS 0, pH 6.8), for soft-water fish and shrimp.
Water comes in through pipes, buckets or a water source block next to it (sea water too). For each part of RO water three parts of waste water leave - into a pipe or tank below, or down the drain.
It simply runs without power, slowly; with a power option on and FE its pressure pump makes it four times faster.
Needs a membrane and a prefilter; both wear out. Empty bucket or pipes take the RO water out (fluid bettacraft:ro_water).
info.bettacraft.ro_water_bucket:
Reverse osmosis water: nothing dissolved (TDS 0, pH 6.8). Into a tank it is a water change that softens the water; mix it with normal water or remineralising salt for the right hardness.
Poured into the world it is plain water. Other mods store it as the fluid bettacraft:ro_water.
info.bettacraft.rotala_hra:
A Rotala with narrow leaves that turn orange and pink under strong light. Grows well only with CO2.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate; grows up to the water surface. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 3 days to full size with strong light (a lit tank light), nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in swamps, sometimes the aquarium net in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it forms side shoots; at the surface it shades the tank.
info.bettacraft.rotala_rotundifolia:
A fast stem plant with small round leaves; the tips turn pink-red under strong light.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate; grows up to the water surface. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 2.5 days to full size with strong light (a lit tank light), nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in swamps, sometimes in a bottle of swamp water; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it forms side shoots; at the surface it shades the tank.
info.bettacraft.rotala_wallichii:
Fine needle leaves in whorls with pink tips; needs very strong light, CO2 and soft water.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate; grows up to the water surface. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 3.5 days to full size with very strong light (an LED panel or a high-power LED), nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: rarely when fishing in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it forms side shoots; at the surface it shades the tank.
info.bettacraft.rotifer_culture: Rotifers on phytoplankton: turns into a bottle of rotifers after one in-game day. Start one from phytoplankton and infusoria, then keep it going: a bottle of rotifers and two of phytoplankton make two cultures.
info.bettacraft.rotifers: Tiny live food for the smallest fry. In a reef tank they stay in the water (with phytoplankton) and are the first food of the clownfish larvae; without them only a few larvae survive.
info.bettacraft.sagittaria_subulata:
Dwarf sagittaria: grass-like, narrow leaves; spreads quickly by runners.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate (the interior floor with a substrate, sand, gravel or dirt). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 4 days to full size with little light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in rivers, sometimes the aquarium net in rivers; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it sends out runners.
info.bettacraft.salt_water_bottle: Use a glass bottle on water in an ocean. Mix it with artemia cysts for an artemia hatchery.
info.bettacraft.salvinia:
A robust floating fern with small paired, hairy leaves. Medium growth.
Grows with light and nutrients, forms offshoots and takes up waste.
Find it: the wandering trader sells it, fishing in swamps.
Take plants out: right-click the surface with an empty hand or an aquarium net; net + sneak thins the whole tank out by half.
info.bettacraft.sarracenia:
A carnivorous plant of the bogs: upright trumpets with a red hood, in which insects drown. Tolerates cool air.
Swamp and shore: 55-100 % humidity, 10-30 °C, strong light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in swamps and mangroves.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.sea_salt:
Salt of the sea with its minerals (calcium too).
Right-click a tank: one portion turns a bucket (1000 mB) of its water into sea water; sneak to add all it needs for 35 ‰.
From a bucket of sea water (crafting) or the wandering trader.
Fresh water dilutes the salt again, evaporation leaves it behind: top up a reef tank with fresh water.
info.bettacraft.sea_water_bucket:
Sea water with 35 ‰ salt and the calcium of the sea.
Fill an empty bucket in an ocean or at a beach, or craft a water bucket with sea salt.
Poured into a tank it makes it a salt water tank; in the world it is plain water.
Draining a salt water tank fills buckets of sea water.
info.bettacraft.sedum:
A low carpet of small, fleshy leaves that turn red in strong light, with tiny yellow flowers. Tortoises graze it.
Dry and hot: 10-55 % humidity, 20-38 °C, strong light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (side shoots) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in deserts, badlands and savannas.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.selaginella:
A spikemoss: a low carpet of feathery, fern-like shoots for the floor of a humid terrarium.
Tropical and humid: 65-100 % humidity, 20-30 °C, little light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (side shoots) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in the lush caves.
Shears: divide the clump (half of it as a plant); breaking a piece of the moss divides it too.
info.bettacraft.shell_food:
Shell food: hard food with crushed shells. It sinks; puffers crack it and wear their teeth down (like on snails), the other fish eat it like granules.
Made in the food maker from bone meal, fish and dried kelp.
info.bettacraft.shrimp_food:
Shrimp food: sinks to the shrimp, crayfish and snails (the fish leave it), twice the food of a leftover pellet, with calcium for the moult.
Made in the food maker.
info.bettacraft.soft_rush:
A rush of upright, round, dark green stems with brown flower tufts near their tips.
Swamp and shore: 50-100 % humidity, 15-30 °C, medium light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (runners) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in swamps and mangroves.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.spawning_cave: Fired clay for a spawning cave. Seven of it make the spawning cave decoration; in the tank interior you can also build your own caves (20 or more connected blocks count as a cave).
info.bettacraft.spawning_mop: Green wool strands of a spawning mop. Three and a stone make the spawning mop decoration. Tetras and rasboras scatter their eggs into it, where the adults cannot reach most of them.
info.bettacraft.sponge_filter: An air-driven filter for the tank interior: needs an air pump. Keeps 12 water blocks clean, aerates a little and never sucks in young animals: the filter for breeding tanks.
info.bettacraft.spray_bar: An outlet in the tank interior: a wide, soft current along a wall.
info.bettacraft.stainless_steel_ingot: Stainless steel for pipes and the water devices. Melted in the crucible from 4 iron ingots, coal and nether quartz (3 ingots), or in the machines of Mekanism, EnderIO, Create (heated mixing) and Thermal. Steel of other mods is no stainless steel.
info.bettacraft.stainless_steel_pipe: Like the glass pipe, but carries 250 mB/t (enough for the multiblock filter's 100 mB/t). A network of both kinds carries what its weakest pipe carries. It joins every neighbour that fits on every side; the pipe wrench closes a side. Sneak-right-click a pipe with it: both run in one block (a bundle, up to four). Placed in a tank interior it is an interior pipe.
info.bettacraft.staurogyne_repens:
A low, bushy carpet of short shoots with small lanceolate leaves; undemanding.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 4.5 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in jungles, sometimes the aquarium net in jungle water; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it sends out runners.
info.bettacraft.steel_leader: Steel leader: hold it in the other hand while fishing with any rod. Now and then a big fish of the water bites instead of the normal catch and goes into an empty transport tub.
info.bettacraft.sump:
A small tank in the cabinet under an aquarium: put it into the sump slot of the cabinet (between the heater slots and the air pump).
Its water counts with the tank (0.5 blocks each): the waste, the nitrate and the dosed values change more slowly, and there is room for more animals. Its return pump runs like an external filter (with FE where the tank needs it).
The button above its slot opens the chambers: two heaters or coolers, a protein skimmer, two filter media and the refugium (Chaetomorpha and a tank light). A level sensor or a dosing pump next to the cabinet serves the tank above.
info.bettacraft.sundew:
A small carnivorous plant: round leaves covered in red, glistening tentacles that catch insects; a flower stalk in the middle. Redder in strong light.
Swamp and shore: 55-100 % humidity, 15-30 °C, strong light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (offsets around it) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in swamps and mangroves; from the wandering trader.
Shears: take an offset (a small rooted plant).
info.bettacraft.swamp_sedge:
A sedge of the shore: a tuft of narrow, arching blades that spreads by runners. Good for the bank of a paludarium.
Swamp and shore: 50-100 % humidity, 15-30 °C, medium light. Plant it on soil, sand or gravel on the land of a terrarium or paludarium: it grows there by the light, the humidity and the air temperature, spreads (runners) and keeps the air humid; in a bad climate it languishes. Outside a tank it is a decoration that does not grow.
Find it: in swamps and mangroves; from short grass; from the aquarist.
Shears: cut cuttings, inside or from outside on the tank where you look.
info.bettacraft.swamp_water_bottle:
Use a glass bottle on water in a swamp.
Smelt it (furnace, smoker or campfire) to hatch mosquito larvae, or mix it with seagrass or leaves for an infusoria culture.
info.bettacraft.tank:
Craft from 6 glass of one kind and 3 iron ingots: the tank shows the texture of that glass, connected across the whole tank.
Clear glass tank: 6 (vanilla) glass, 1 iron nugget in the middle and 3 iron ingots below. A single vanilla-glass tank converts between both styles in the crafting grid.
Place tanks of the same glass and style next to each other to build one large tank of any connected shape (L, T, steps; up to 16x16x16).
Fill it with water buckets: 1 bucket = 1000 mB, from 50% on animals can move in.
Right-click: tank menu. Shift + right-click: enter the interior to decorate it.
info.bettacraft.tank_lid:
Lay it on a top block of a tank: that block no longer loses water by evaporation.
The feeder and lights cover the block they stand on as well; the light bar can also lie on the lid itself.
info.bettacraft.tank_light:
Place it on or above a tank, or onto a lid on a tank (it lies on the lid in the same block); neighbouring lights join into one bar.
Light level 15, the weakest of the three light tiers (stronger: LED panel, high-power LED). A redstone signal switches the whole bar off; dimmer and daylight timer in the tank menu (tab Devices).
Dye it (right-click dyes the whole bar, or in the crafting grid): 16 colours tint the water, the plants get the same light.
info.bettacraft.tank_net:
Takes floating plants off the water surface of a tank and small animals out of it. Right-click the tank: the plant (or the shrimp, crayfish, snail, clutch or shed shell) where you look comes out, from above as well as from the side through the glass. Animals go into a fish bag.
Sneak + right-click: thins the floating plants out by half (lily pads stay), like the button on the plants tab of the tank menu.
In open water (rivers, swamps, mangroves, beaches, jungle, caves) it catches shrimp, snails and frogs into an empty fish bag; that wears it a little. In rivers, jungle water and swamps it now and then brings up an aquarium plant from the bottom, on a reef a piece of coral.
Craft: four string in a square with a stick below on the left.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.agassiz_dwarf_c:
Agassiz's Dwarf Cichlid (Apistogramma agassizii) from the soft blackwater of the Amazon basin.
The male is bluish with an orange and blue framed spade tail (Fire Red: red fins); the female yellow with a dark stripe.
One male with one or more females, 24–29 °C, soft water, water: sensitive. Counts 0.7 fish in the stocking.
Cave brooder: every female claims a small cave (coconut shell, slate cave, spawning cave) and guards eggs and young there.
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.angelfish:
Angelfish (Pterophyllum scalare) from the calm, plant-rich waters of the Amazon.
A tall, flat cichlid with huge fins: silver with black bars; bred as Black, Marble, Koi and Platinum.
Alone, as a pair or a group in a big tall tank, 24–30 °C, water: average. Counts 2 fish in the stocking.
Open brooder: the pair spawns on a broad leaf or the glass and guards eggs and young.
Eats small fish (neons, embers, mosquito rasboras) and shrimp; not with bettas.
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.arapaima:
Arapaima (Arapaima gigas), the giant of the Amazon floodplains: a long, round body whose scales turn red towards the tail; 2 m in the game (wild up to 3 m).
Big animal: needs a tank of at least 24 × 12 × 6 blocks and 800 water blocks each.
An air breather: comes up to the surface for air every few minutes and does not mind low oxygen. 24–31 °C, soft to medium water. Eats fish, bettas and shrimp. Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: large net or steel leader in jungle water (into a transport tub); very rarely wild there.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.archerfish:
Banded archerfish (Toxotes jaculatrix) from the mangroves and river mouths from India to northern Australia.
Silver-white with four or five black wedge bars, big eyes, a pointed head, the dorsal fin far back; about 12 cm in a tank.
Small group of 3 or more, 24–30 °C, fresh to brackish water (best brackish). Counts 2 fish in the stocking. Swims under the surface.
Shoots insects off the leaves above the water with a jet of water: fruit flies let out over an open tank, insects at the plants above it (a paludarium, a mangrove crown). Now and then it splashes a player who leans over the tank.
Does not breed in a tank. Catch: aquarium net in mangrove swamps, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.bamboo_shark:
Brownbanded bamboo shark (Chiloscyllium punctatum) of the Indo-West Pacific reefs: a slender, brown bottom shark with barbels and two dorsal fins far back; 1 m.
Big animal: needs a sea water tank of at least 12 × 6 × 3 blocks and 100 water blocks each; lies on the ground under ledges by day and hunts at night.
22–28 °C. Eats shrimp, crabs and small fish.
Lays leathery egg cases (mermaid's purses) under the decoration; each pup hatches after about ten days, only when the tank has room for it (size rule).
Catch: large net or steel leader in warm and lukewarm oceans (into a transport tub); rarely wild there.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.banggai_cardina:
Banggai Cardinalfish (Pterapogon kauderni) from the shallow bays of the Banggai islands (Indonesia).
Silver with three black bars, long fins with white dots; calm and slow.
As a pair, 24–28 °C, sea water, water: normal. Counts 0.8 fish in the stocking.
Mouthbrooder: the female passes her eggs to the male, who carries them in his mouth; the young come out fully formed (no fry food needed). The easy reef fish to breed.
Catch: aquarium net in warm oceans, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.black_molly:
Black Molly (Poecilia sphenops) from the rivers and coasts of Central America, in fresh and brackish water.
Velvet black; bred as Dalmatian (white with black spots) and Gold.
In a group of 3 or more, 22–30 °C, hard water, fresh or brackish (up to 18 ppt), water: average. Counts 0.8 fish in the stocking.
Grazes a little algae. Livebearer: bears live young; a breeding box saves them from the adults.
Catch: aquarium net in mangrove swamps and rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.black_phantom_t:
Black Phantom Tetra (Hyphessobrycon megalopterus) from the rivers of central Brazil.
Smoky silver with a black shoulder patch; the male has big black fins, the female red ones.
In a shoal of 6 or more, 22–28 °C, soft water, water: average. Counts 0.4 fish in the stocking.
The males show off to each other without harm. Egg scatterer: eggs into fine plants, moss or a spawning mop.
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water and rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.blacktip_reef_s:
Blacktip reef shark (Carcharhinus melanopterus) of the shallow Indo-Pacific reefs: a grey shark with black tips on its fins; 1.6 m in the game.
Big animal: needs a sea water tank of at least 20 × 10 × 5 blocks and 410 water blocks each; it has to keep swimming to breathe and never rests.
24–30 °C. A predator: eats every fish up to its own mouth size, bettas and shrimp. Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: large net or steel leader in warm oceans (into a transport tub); very rarely wild there.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.bolivian_ram:
Bolivian Ram (Mikrogeophagus altispinosus) from the Río Mamoré and Guaporé in Bolivia and Brazil.
Bigger and hardier than the ram: beige with a yellow front, a black spot in the middle and red fin edges.
As a pair, 22–29 °C, water: average. Counts 1 fish in the stocking.
Open brooder: the pair cleans a flat stone and guards eggs and young.
Catch: aquarium net in rivers and jungle water, wandering trader (rare).
info.bettacraft.tankmate.bristlenose_ple:
Bristlenose Pleco (Ancistrus sp.) from South American rivers; the aquarium form is bred everywhere.
The best algae eater of the tankmates; males grow bristles on the snout. Also albino and super red.
Fine on its own, 21–28 °C, water: hardy. Counts 1.2 fish in the stocking.
Spawns in a cave, the male guards.
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.bronze_cory:
Bronze Cory (Corydoras aeneus) from the rivers east of the Andes, from Colombia to the Rio de la Plata.
Metallic green-bronze flanks, a pale belly; the most common cory of the trade and one of the hardiest. Albino and Gold Laser (an orange-gold stripe along the back) are recessive bred forms.
Shoal of 6 or more, 20–28 °C, water: hardy. Counts 0.6 fish in the stocking.
Glues its eggs to the glass (after a cool water change).
Catch: aquarium net in rivers and jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.cardinal_tetra:
Cardinal Tetra (Paracheirodon axelrodi) from the Rio Negro and Orinoco (Brazil, Venezuela), warm blackwater.
Like the neon, but the red runs the whole length of the belly; likes it warmer, good with bettas. Bred form (recessive): Gold.
Shoal of 6 or more, 24–30 °C, water: very sensitive. Counts 0.4 fish in the stocking.
Scatters its eggs (fine plants, spawning mop).
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.celestial_pearl:
Celestial Pearl Danio (Celestichthys margaritatus) from small, plant-filled ponds in the hills of Myanmar.
Tiny, blue-grey with golden pearl spots; the male has an orange belly and red-orange fins with black bars.
In a shoal of 6 or more, 20–26 °C, soft water, water: sensitive. Counts 0.15 fish in the stocking.
Shy, stays low between the plants; fine with a betta. Egg scatterer: eggs into moss.
Catch: aquarium net in swamps, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.cherry_barb:
Cherry Barb (Rohanella titteya) from the shady forest streams of Sri Lanka.
A small, calm barb with a dark stripe along the side; the male turns cherry red, the female stays beige.
In a shoal of 6 or more, 22–28 °C, water: average. Counts 0.4 fish in the stocking.
Peaceful, fine with a betta. Egg scatterer: eggs into fine plants, moss or a spawning mop.
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water and rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.chocolate_goura:
Chocolate Gourami (Sphaerichthys osphromenoides) from the peat swamps of Malaysia, Sumatra and Borneo.
Chocolate brown with cream bands and yellow-edged fins.
In a group of 4 or more, 25–30 °C, only very soft, acid water (peat, almond leaves), water: very sensitive. Counts 0.5 fish in the stocking.
A labyrinth fish. A mouthbrooder: the female carries the eggs in her mouth and spits out free-swimming young after some days.
Catch: aquarium net in swamps and jungle water, wandering trader (rare).
info.bettacraft.tankmate.clown_loach:
Clown Loach (Chromobotia macracanthus) from the rivers of Borneo and Sumatra.
Orange with three black bands, gets big, wants a group and eats snails. Does not breed in tanks.
Shoal of 5 or more, 25–30 °C, water: sensitive. Counts 2.5 fish in the stocking.
Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: aquarium net in swamps, jungle water, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.cockatoo_cichli:
Cockatoo Dwarf Cichlid (Apistogramma cacatuoides) from the upper Amazon in Peru and Colombia.
The male carries a tall, spiky crest and a lyre tail with red marks (Double Red, Orange Flash); the smaller female turns yellow when she guards.
One male with one or more females, 22–29 °C, water: average. Counts 0.8 fish in the stocking.
Cave brooder: every female claims a small cave (coconut shell, slate cave, spawning cave) and guards eggs and young there.
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water and rivers, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.cownose_ray:
Cownose ray (Rhinoptera bonasus) of the western Atlantic: a brown ray with a notched "cow nose" head that swims in schools; 1 m.
Big animal: needs a sea water tank of at least 12 × 6 × 3 blocks and 100 water blocks each; keep three or more: they follow each other through the open water with slow wing beats.
18–28 °C. Cracks clams and snails, eats shrimp.
Livebearing: one big pup after a long pregnancy, only when the tank has room for it (size rule).
Catch: large net or steel leader in lukewarm and warm oceans (into a transport tub); rarely wild there, in small schools.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.discus:
Discus (Symphysodon aequifasciatus) from the warm, very soft water of the Amazon.
The king of the aquarium: a round, flat disc, brown with blue lines in the wild; bred as Red Turquoise, Pigeon Blood and Blue Diamond.
In a group of 3 or more, 27–32 °C (best 30), very soft water, water: very sensitive. Counts 2.5 fish in the stocking.
Open brooder: the pair spawns on a broad leaf or the glass; the young feed on their parents' skin for days and die without them.
Catch: aquarium net in jungle water, wandering trader (rare).
info.bettacraft.tankmate.dwarf_chain_loa:
Dwarf Chain Loach (Ambastaia sidthimunki) from the rivers of Thailand and Laos.
A small loach, pale with a chain of dark links along the side and back.
In a group of 6 or more, 24–29 °C, water: sensitive. Counts 0.4 fish in the stocking.
Eats snails. Swims in the lower water, also in the open. Does not breed in a tank.
Catch: aquarium net in rivers, wandering trader (rare).
info.bettacraft.tankmate.dwarf_gourami:
Dwarf Gourami (Trichogaster lalius) from plant-rich waters of India and Bangladesh.
Blue and red striped males with long feelers; a labyrinth fish like the betta - male gouramis and male bettas fight.
Fine on its own, 24–29 °C, water: average. Counts 1 fish in the stocking.
Builds a foam nest.
Catch: aquarium net in swamps, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.dwarf_puffer:
Dwarf Puffer (Carinotetraodon travancoricus) from the rivers of Kerala in south-west India; the smallest puffer, also called pea puffer.
Yellow-green with dark blotches and big, moving eyes; the male has a dark line along the belly.
Alone or a species group without bettas, 22–29 °C, water: sensitive. Counts 0.4 fish in the stocking.
Eats snails (bladder and ramshorn snails first) and needs them or hard food (shell food): without them its teeth overgrow. Nips the fins of long-finned fish.
Egg scatterer: lays its eggs into moss and fine plants.
Catch: aquarium net in rivers and swamps, wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.tankmate.dwarf_seahorse:
